# stdx/assert

> Assertion: assert cond stops the program if cond is false.

truck [stdx](../stdx.md) · [source](../../../registry/stdx/assert.pkg)

```
assert len(items) > 0
assert total == 42
```

If the condition is false, the program writes where the assertion is
to stderr and exits with status 2, like other runtime errors:

```
assertion failed at app.pkg:12:3
```

It writes with a system call, so output buffered by `rt/io` and not yet
flushed is lost. The position comes from `{@pos}` in the expansion:

```
if !cond
  syscall(1, 2, cstr("assertion failed at "), 20)
  syscall(1, 2, cstr("app.pkg:12:3"), len("app.pkg:12:3"))
  syscall(1, 2, cstr("\n"), 1)
  syscall(60, 2)
end
```

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`

```
assert {cond: expr bool}
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `cond` | expression | `bool` |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
if !{cond}
syscall(1, 2, cstr("assertion failed at "), 20)
syscall(1, 2, cstr({@pos}), len({@pos}))
syscall(1, 2, cstr("\n"), 1)
syscall(60, 2)
end
```
